messages:
maria: heads up — after the torch.compile + cudagraphs warmup tweak i pushed yesterday i'm seeing intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes on the production GPU pool. reproducible on canary.
chris: any recent autotune or kernel-selection changes in that deploy?
maria: only the dynamic-shape handshake change + we started capturing graphs slightly earlier in the step loop. suspect interaction with seqlen-dependent kernel picks.
alex: can you paste a tiny nsys/snippet and the request distribution?
maria: logging snippets below, short repro attached. latency p95 jumps from ~60ms to ~230ms randomly across requests. distro: mostly seqlen 16/64 mixed.
```
# nsys summary (truncated)
Time(%)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Min  Max  Kernel
45.2     1200   0.18    0.01  4.2  fused_attn_fp16_sm80
32.1      600   0.52    0.03  12.9  matmul_autotuned_variant_B
15.7      300   0.90    0.05  200.5  matmul_autotuned_variant_A
```
maria: note matmul_autotuned_variant_A shows massive tail for some traces.
priya: variants A/B are architecture-aware picks from the autotuner, right? A is optimized for long seqlen, B for short.
chris: that suggests graph capture + dynshape is causing different kernel to be chosen mid-flight. maybe cudagraph replay is picking a path with larger workspace allocation and causing eviction.
alex: does the KV cache get rebuilt between captures? if kv buffers are resized, caffeinated cudagraphs might be invalidated and fallback to a slower kernel.
maria: kv cache stays persistent but on mixed batching we've seen small reallocations during warmup. suspect handshake: early capture for seqlen16 then later recv seqlen64 -> capture mismatch.
sam: can you run with AUTOTUNE_VERBOSE=1 and RT_LOG=capture to get kernel-selection trace? would show why A vs B chosen.
maria: ran that — attaching trimmed trace: 
```
[autotune] seqlen_hist: {16: 820, 64: 180}
[autotune] selected kernel: matmul_variant_B for batch_signature=... (prob 0.88)
[graph] capture: cudagraph_id=42 created for seqlen=16, workspace=8MB
[replay] cudagraph_id=42 replayed for seqlen=64 -> fallback to variant_A (path mismatch)
```
priya: oh interesting, replaying a seqlen16 graph for seqlen64? that's unsafe — should have invalidated. why didn't it?
maria: because we changed the capture-safe check to be looser (to reduce capture churn). looks like it reduced churn but introduced cross-seqlen reuse.
chris: Could explain the tail — variant_A requires different tiling and ends up launching many more blocks for some batch shapes, plus extra syncs.
alex: quick workaround: tighten capture-safety (disallow seqlen <=/>= mixing) OR force per-seqlen kernel selection before cudagraph replay. both doable as short-term.
sam: for repro, try this small script (python) that alternates seqlen 16/64 with torch.compile + set cudagraphs=True and warmup=1 — should reproduce locally:
```
# repro.py (very small)
import torch
from runtime import serve_step
model = load_small()
model = torch.compile(model)
for i in range(200):
  seqlen = 16 if i % 3 else 64
  x = torch.randn(1, seqlen, 1024, device='cuda')
  out = serve_step(model, x, use_cudagraph=True)
```
maria: confirmed repro with that script on my devbox. attaching perf traces.
priya: is there a kernel cache key that includes seqlen? if not we should add it. that will force distinct profiles and avoid cross-replay.
chris: adding seqlen to key is safe but increases kernel-variants stored — tradeoff. maybe add only for kernels where workspace/tiling is seqlen-sensitive.
alex: also check batching heuristics: the batch sampler sometimes coalesces requests with different seqlens into one micro-batch then we unbatch into different internal partitions. that could cause ambiguous profiles at capture time.
sam: good point. we should also log batch-partitioning decisions to see if the sampler is the trigger.
maria: for immediate mitigation i've rolled back the looser capture-safety in canary and p95 dropped back to baseline. but we should plan longer fix.
priya: proposed permanent fixes: 1) include seqlen/signature in kernel cache key (selectively), 2) strengthen capture invalidation rules when workspace/tiling mismatches, 3) add a flag to force kernel-selection pre-replay.
chris: agree. also add a small regression test in runtime-tests that alternates seqlen during warmup and asserts no variant flip inside a single cudagraph replay.
alex: i'll open a PR with the selective key change + verbose metrics. will add an opt-in feature flag.
maria: thanks — tagging infra-bot to run extended canary: @infra-bot canary-run: runtime-canary-2025-kernel-fix
infra-bot: acknowledged. queued job runtime-canary-2025-kernel-fix on gpunode-12, ETA 18m. :rocket:
priya: assignable owners? alex for kernel-key, chris for capture-invalidation, sam for batch-sampler logging. i'll put tasks in the runtime epic.
maria: thanks all. i'll leave traces in /tmp/repro-2012367890 and follow up if the canary shows residual tails. :thumbsup:
